Commentary.Commentary: Welcome back for England's second crack with the bat. The Indians form a huddle as Shubman Gill provides the final words before they spread out to the field. Out walk the two English openers, Zak Crawley and Ben Duckett. Jasprit Bumrah, already having snagged a 5-fer in the first innings, will obviously open the attack for the visitors. England are trying all their tactics to stall and reduce it to a single over before Stumps. But finally, Crawley is ready to face. Here we go...
.... THIRD INNINGS ...

Well then, with around 5 minutes of the day's play remaining, just a couple of overs could be squeezed in. India will hope that Jasprit Bumrah provides his magic in this space of time. A very nervy final minutes of day's play coming up, folks. Strap yourselves in.

England, no doubt, had to toil very hard in the boiling London heat, bowling around 120 overs. But with the second new ball taken, they managed to get just enough seam movement to trouble the batters and after Ravindra Jadeja's wicket, it just took England exactly 6 overs to wrap up the Indian lower order. The highlight of this English bowling attack was Jofra Archer who delivered literal thunderbolts at the batters and produced a gem of a delivery to dismiss Jaiswal in the very third ball of his return in the whites. Ben Stokes too, delivered a highly testing spell, but it was Chris Woakes who chipped in with three wickets to his name.

Looking at the Indian scorecard, contributions have come from almost all. Barring Yashasvi Jaiswal and Shubman Gill, everyone in the top 8 managed to cross 20 runs. The key to this innings has been the partnerships as four partnerships were worth 50 runs or more, including a 141-run marathon stand between KL Rahul and Rishabh Pant. The Indian batting more or less revolved around KL Rahul's innings, laden with class and flair as he became the second Indian batter to register at least two centuries at Lord's. The lower order thrust was provided by Ravindra Jadeja's 72 and Washington Sundar's crucial 23 as well.

After almost three days of gruelling, there's absolutely nothing that separates the two sides as the scores remain level at Lord's. England will get around 7 minutes to bat. Ben Duckett and Zak Crawley have already sprinted into the dressing room to pad up.

In a bit of a setback for England, Shoaib Bashir walked off the field after taking a blow to his left hand. It appeared to be a dislocation at the time and the hosts will be hoping he can return for the final session. The Dukes ball typically starts to move around the 12-over mark once the lacquer wears off, and England will be eager to exploit that window, which is around the corner. India, with the deficit down to 71, will look to Jadeja and Reddy to carry on the recovery and push towards parity and beyond. Back in a bit for the final session of the day.

Nitish Kumar Reddy was tested by a fiery spell from Jofra Archer operating at full tilt and survived a couple of run out chances, with Ollie Pope missing direct-hit opportunities on both occasions. With the second new ball looming, a pivotal phase awaited both sides. Archer steamed in from one end and continued to send down thunderbolts, but as a unit, England lacked a bit of discipline with the new ball and did not quite test the two batters enough. The running between the wickets continued to be iffy between Jadeja and Reddy, but the pair managed to hold fort and saw the session through.

A moment of brilliance from Ben Stokes, right on the stroke of Lunch, had given England the breakthrough they were desperate for. Their spirits lifted even further with the dismissal of KL Rahul, who fell immediately after reaching his hundred. Wickets on either side of the Lunch break triggered panic in the Indian camp, and it showed in their running between the wickets.

SESSION SUMMARY - 25.3 overs, 68 runs, 1 wicket. Another session in this gripping Test that ebbed and flowed. After a frenetic start, India would have feared worse, but Nitish Kumar Reddy and Ravindra Jadeja managed to steer them to calmer waters. England sensed blood in the water and did create run-out opportunities, but couldn’t capitalise on the chances that came their way.

Commentary.Commentary: DRINKS BREAK. The Indian batters have looked like cats on a hot tin roof ever since Pant’s and Rahul's dismissals. Restless, edgy, and vulnerable. That Pant run out seems to have sparked a string of nervy moments, with two more close calls where the batters could have been run out had the throws been on target. Meanwhile, Jofra Archer stormed back into the attack, sending thunderbolts at the batters and reigniting the English charge. Jadeja has looked good, while Nitish is still searching for stability with the bat, but this partnership for India will be very crucial. Also, it’s worth recalling how England clawed their way up from 271/7, with the tail wagging fiercely to tack on 116 valuable runs for the last three wickets. India will be hoping for a similar act of defiance from their lower order, not just to level the scores but to inch ahead. With Bashir off the field, Root remains England's prime spin resource. And now, the second new ball is available for England. Will the hosts opt for it? Yes, the new ball has been taken straightaway. Brydon Carse (16-2-69-0) to continue after the break.

Commentary.Commentary: Welcome back for the post-Lunch session at Lord's. Bright sunshine welcomes the umpires and players back on the field. Ben Stokes leads his men as the English players spread out to the field. KL Rahul, unbeaten on 98, will be joined by Ravindra Jadeja at the crease as Rishabh Pant was run out just before the Lunch break. Shoaib Bashir (8.3-1-33-0) to complete his over. Here we go...
... DAY 3, SECOND SESSION ...

Well then, another session has flown by in this Lord's Test. England still have their fair share of struggles to be nursed, though. Their front line of attack, including Archer and Woakes, carried purpose and precision, testing the batters with sharp lines. But, with the second string failing to maintain pressure, England may have to lean heavily on Shoaib Bashir to extract something from the wearing surface, especially as the cracks begin to open and the rhythm shifts in favour of spin. Coming into the afternoon session, England's aim will be to pick a couple of more quick wickets and not allow India to get back in rhythm. While the tourists will be keen to string a few more partnerships, as the deficit is still considerably high. This Indian batting will largely circle around KL Rahul, who is on the brink of another century, but will need stability at the other end. An exciting second session is on the cards. Play resumes at 6.10 pm IST (12.40 pm GMT). Join us then!

Pant had his share of discomfort against the rising deliveries, with his injured left index finger clearly affecting control. Yet, alongside KL Rahul, he kept the scoreboard ticking, bringing up a valiant fifty as the partnership crossed past 100. But just as India looked set to reach lunch without damage, a calamitous mix-up ended the 141-run stand. Pant was run out moments before the break, leaving India 139 runs adrift.

With conventional avenues closing, England resorted to the short-ball tactic, hoping to stir discomfort. Also, with England's third seamer, Brydon Carse, proving to be a bit costly on the docile pitch, Stokes had to bring himself on. However, on such a slowish deck, this plan fell flat. Those short balls were easily dealt with, as the batters just had that extra cushion of time to deal with those.

England’s bowlers, growing restless, made a couple of appeals for a change of ball. Archer showed his discontent early, but the replacement didn’t come until after the drinks break. Rahul, unfazed and fluent, anchored the stand while Pant, nursing his bruises, threw in moments of audacity, rushing down at the quicks and unfurling his cheeky scoop shots with typical unpredictability.

The end of the session might have been very disappointing for the Indians, but they began the day well. Both KL Rahul and Rishabh Pant walked out with quiet resolve, soaking in the early pressure as Archer and Woakes strung together a disciplined spell of dot balls. The pitch offered little in return, and once the ball began to soften, the Indian pair opened up, collecting boundaries and easing into their rhythm. In the opening hour, they carved out 52 runs across 13 overs, steadily chipping away at England’s lead.

SESSION SUMMARY - 22.3 Overs, 103 Runs, 1 Wicket. Smiles all around the English camp. As after a long toil in the morning heat, almost going wicketless, this Rishabh Pant's run out, right at the stroke of Lunch, has injected a fresh energy in this team. A pretty needless risk from him and he would be absolutely kicking himself as Pant walks frustratingly through the Lord's Long Room.

OUT! RUN OUT! Ben Stokes, you beauty! The golden arm of Stokes delivers for England in the form of a direct hit for a change. A brutal blow for India right at the stroke of Lunch. From around the wicket, this is tossed up, on off, Rishabh leans forward and taps it with soft hands in front of cover. Pant hesitates at first before committing to the single. Stokes swoops in, picks the ball up and turns around. In one motion, he releases the throw and scores a direct hit at the bowling end. The third umpire is called into action. Rishabh stretches forward but the replays show that he is short of his crease. A dive would have probably saved Pant but he decided not to and ultimately paid the price. Stokes lets out a roar and he is pumped up. Rishabh Pant falls for 74 (112). At Lunch on Day 3, India are 248/4, trailing by 139 runs.

PITCH REPORT - Pitchside at Lord's on Day 3, Raunak Kapoor notes cooler temperatures under clear skies. Deep Dasgupta joins him and observes that the batting surface has been repaired, which wasn't done in the first two days, which is a positive sign. He notes a few minor footmarks beginning to appear. Then highlights a crack that caused inconsistent bounce and mentions the presence of grass, which could keep bowlers interested. As they move toward the Nursery End, Deep points out more cracks and emphasizes the influence of the slope. Despite those challenges, he believes it remains a good batting surface that could slow down later in the day. With the ball slightly older, batting may become easier, and the roller’s effect in the first 30 to 45 minutes should help the ball come nicely onto the bat.

The over rate has been slow, and despite the extra half hour being used on both days, only 83 overs were bowled on Day 1 and 72.3 on Day 2. Frequent ball changes, with the Dukes going out of shape too soon, have caused multiple interruptions. Rahul will be central to India’s hopes of narrowing the deficit, while England will look to Archer and Co. to exploit the morning conditions. All in all, we have an intriguing day in prospect. Stick around!

As for India, after the early inroads created by Jasprit Bumrah, it looked like they might be able to restrict England to around 320. However, the dropped catch of Jamie Smith when he was on 5 proved costly. In reply, KL Rahul held firm at one end and saw out the day with Rishabh Pant, who showed great grit while batting through the pain of an injured left hand.

England had a shaky start to Day 2, slipping to 271/7, but the lower order bailed them out of trouble. The last three wickets added 116 valuable runs, with fifties from Jamie Smith and Brydon Carse lifting the total to 387. Jofra Archer set the tone with the ball, and England struck at key moments, including the prized wicket of Shubman Gill, just as partnerships threatened to develop.

Day 2 at Lord’s was special for several reasons. It was Red for Ruth Day, with the iconic venue draped in red in support of the Ruth Strauss Foundation. This Test was billed as the return of two champion pacers, Jasprit Bumrah and Jofra Archer, and both delivered. Archer bowled with serious pace and struck with his third ball on return. Bumrah, meanwhile, produced the much-anticipated performance at Lord’s that earned him a place on the honours board. Joe Root, with his 37th Test hundred, climbed to fifth on the all-time centuries list. Later in the day, with a left-handed stunner, Root went past Rahul Dravid’s tally to become the fielder with the most catches in Test cricket, claiming his 211th.

Hello, one and all! The moving day dawns at the Home of Cricket, and given how tightly contested the first two days have been, today promises to be no different. Which camp would you rather be in at the moment? It has to be England. They posted a sizable first-innings total and followed it up by picking up three wickets. Scoring has been tough given the sluggish nature of the surface, and with 242 runs still needed to catch up with the hosts, India have it all to do.
... DAY 3, SESSION 1 ...

Two absorbing days of Test cricket have seen both teams trading blows. There was plenty of talk on the opening day about the pitch being on the slower side and the edges not carrying. But come the morning of Day 2, the surface had noticeably quickened up. It remains to be seen how it behaves on Day 3, but even with the older ball, there has been enough on offer to keep the pacers interested. Undoubtedly, KL Rahul will hold the key for India, and they will be hoping he can replicate his 2021 heroics at Lord’s, where he scored a ton. As for England, after a good night’s rest, their pacers will be raring to go and will look to exploit the morning conditions. Saturday, 12th July will be Day 3 of this Lord's Test, with the first ball to be bowled at 3.30 pm IST (10 am GMT). As always, we will be here nice and early for the build-up. Until then, take care and goodbye!

Nair got off to a decent start, as did Shubman Gill but neither could kick on. Chris Woakes, who looked off-colour in his opening spell, returned to the attack and the move to bring Jamie Smith up to the stumps for the Indian skipper worked wonders for the hosts. Rishabh Pant walked in with an injured left index finger and managed to find boundaries against Shoaib Bashir, though he was visibly in discomfort at times. KL Rahul, meanwhile, continued to look solid at the other end, and the duo ensured there was no further damage before stumps.

While Smith couldn’t carry on for long after lunch, Carse continued to frustrate the Indians and went on to register his maiden Test fifty. His dismissal eventually brought the curtains down on England’s innings at 387, with Bumrah claiming his first five-wicket haul at Lord’s. Jofra Archer struck with his third ball on Test return and breathed fire in his opening spell. However, KL Rahul and Karun Nair managed to weather that early storm.

Day 2 kicked off with high drama. Joe Root, stranded overnight on 99, reached his century with the first ball of the morning but fell soon after. Jasprit Bumrah then produced a fiery three-wicket burst to reduce England to 271/7. The English lower order then staged a spirited fightback. Jamie Smith, dropped on 5, made India pay with another fluent fifty and found solid support from Brydon Carse. Shubman Gill and Co. were visibly unhappy with the changed ball, which they felt was not new enough, and the emotions clearly got to them.

SESSION SUMMARY - 29 overs, 101 runs and 2 wickets. Another slowish day in terms of scoring, where the batters were made to grind hard for their runs, but it was still a captivating day of Test cricket. It was a good day at the office for England, but not so much for India, who have plenty of ground to cover. Ben Stokes and his men will be pleased to have seen the back of Shubman Gill, while the tourists will need a strong response on Day 3.

OUT! EDGED AND GONE! Spectacular grab by Joe Root! On a back of a length, around the off stump, Nair hangs on the back foot and is opened up a bit due to the ball straightening off the deck. Commentary.Commentary: Welcome back for the third and final session of the day. The umpires and players make their way out to the middle as the sun shines bright. KL Rahul and Karun Nair are all set to resume their batting. And it will be the English skipper, Ben Stokes, who will bowl the first over of the session from the Nursery End. Three slips await as Nair gears up to face. Here we go...
... DAY 2, THIRD SESSION ...

Well then, another session has flown by in this third Test. There's still a little bit of seam movement on offer on this deck for the pacers and coming into the third session, the English bowlers will aim to break this brewing partnership between KL Rahul and Karun Nair. It's an important innings from Nair's point of view as he has got the starts in this series, but hasn't converted them into substantial scores. This intriguing battle will continue post-Tea as play resumes in just a few minutes' time. Stay tuned.

Chris Woakes looked a bit erratic as he conceded a few too many runs in the first spell, but he was backed up well by Carse from his end. KL Rahul, though, brought a sense of calm and control, anchoring the innings with smart, percentage-driven batting. Karun Nair has looked edgy at times, getting beaten outside the off stump more than once, but he held firm and has got yet another start.

In reply, India’s innings kicked off with flair as Jaiswal peppered the boundary in the very first over. But his stay was cut short by the sheer pace of Jofra Archer, who looked rhythmical and charged up on his Test return after four years. He gave all his heart and soul, and the Indian batters were evidently caught off guard, struggling to adjust to his cranking pace and lively bounce. His return has seemingly given England the cutting edge they'd been missing. He bowled with sharp pace, used the Lord’s slope to his benefit from the Pavilion End, and got the ball to bounce and nip both ways.

The post-lunch session was England’s lower-order hustle, with Jamie Smith holding fort as the lone recognised batter. However, Brydon Carse offered solid support to him from the other end. The duo stitched together an 84-run stand that frustrated India until Siraj finally broke through. Just when it looked like India would run through the tail, Carse stepped up with a fighting fifty of his own, adding crucial runs and dragging England to a commendable 387. The last three wickets piled on 116 runs for the hosts, which could well prove valuable in the context of the game. Bumrah, on the flip side, claimed his fifth wicket with an absolute peach to dismiss Archer, putting himself on course for a spot on the Lord's honours board.

SESSION SUMMARY - 21.3 Overs, 78 Runs, and 4 wickets. A highly entertaining and engaging afternoon session where the ball has dominated the bat. The scoring rate by both teams has not been brisk by any means, but this Lord's Test has indeed moved quickly on the second day with double the action from the opening day.

A beauty from Woakes to end the session! Wobble seam delivery, on a good length, just outside the off stump, KL Rahul leans ahead for the block but the ball seams away to zip past the outside edge. That will be TEA on Day 2!

OUT! EDGED AND GONE! A dream start to the comeback for Jofra Archer as he draws the first blood pretty early! He bangs it hard on the surface, around middle with the ball deviating away off the deck. Jaiswal opens up and brings his bat in front to defend, but the ball nips away from the surface and takes the thick, healthy outside edge. Flies flat and straight towards the second slip as Harry Brook takes a regulation grab. The Lord's crowd is right behind Archer as he is delighted. India are 13/1 as Jaiswal goes for 13 (8).
Commentary.Howout: c Harry Brook b Jofra Archer
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 1.3: Jofra Archer to Yashasvi Jaiswal, OUT! c Harry Brook b Jofra Archer.

Commentary.Commentary: BEATEN! Good gas from Archer, angling around off, kisses the surface on a length and goes quicker. Jaiswal is late to react and is beaten on the outside edge.
